The First Amendment Act (1951) made this change: Added the Ninth Schedule and enabled specified land-reform protections.

President of India: Elected by an electoral college including elected MPs and elected MLAs of States and specified Union territories; Five years; Thirty-five years.
Vice-President of India: Elected by members of both Houses of Parliament; Five years; Thirty-five years.
Lok Sabha member: Directly elected by voters of a territorial constituency; Normally five years for the House; Twenty-five years.
Rajya Sabha member from a State: Elected by elected members of that State's Legislative Assembly; Six years; Thirty years.
State Legislative Assembly member: Directly elected by the State's voters; Normally five years for the Assembly; Twenty-five years.
State Legislative Council member: Chosen through a mix of elections and nomination prescribed by the Constitution; Six years; Thirty years.
Governor: Appointed by the President; Five years, subject to the President's pleasure; Thirty-five years.
Supreme Court judge: Appointed by the President under the constitutional process; Retirement at sixty-five; Citizenship and prescribed judicial or legal experience.
High Court judge: Appointed by the President under the constitutional process; Retirement at sixty-two; Citizenship and prescribed judicial or legal experience.
Comptroller and Auditor-General: Appointed by the President; Six years or until age sixty-five, whichever is earlier; Qualifications are not fixed by the Constitution.
UPSC Chairperson: Appointed by the President; Six years or until age sixty-five, whichever is earlier; As prescribed within the constitutional framework.
State PSC Chairperson: Appointed by the Governor; Six years or until age sixty-two, whichever is earlier; As prescribed within the constitutional framework.
Attorney General for India: Appointed by the President; During the President's pleasure; Qualified to be a Supreme Court judge.
Advocate General of a State: Appointed by the Governor; During the Governor's pleasure; Qualified to be a High Court judge.
Prime Minister: Appointed by the President; Dependent on confidence of the Lok Sabha; Must meet constitutional membership requirements.
Chief Minister: Appointed by the Governor; Dependent on confidence of the Legislative Assembly; Must meet constitutional membership requirements.
Speaker of the Lok Sabha: Elected by the Lok Sabha from among its members; Normally until immediately before the first meeting of the next Lok Sabha; Must be a Lok Sabha member.
Deputy Speaker of the Lok Sabha: Elected by the Lok Sabha from among its members; Subject to the constitutional rules on vacancy and removal; Must be a Lok Sabha member.
Deputy Chairman of the Rajya Sabha: Elected by the Rajya Sabha from among its members; Subject to membership and constitutional removal rules; Must be a Rajya Sabha member.
Finance Commission: Constituted by the President; Constituted every five years or earlier; Chairperson and four other members.
GST Council: Constituted under Article 279A; A continuing constitutional body; Chaired by the Union Finance Minister.
Election Commission of India: Appointed under the Constitution and applicable law; As prescribed by applicable law; Supervises specified national and State elections.
National Commission for Scheduled Castes: Appointed by the President; As prescribed under the constitutional framework; Safeguards concerning Scheduled Castes.
National Commission for Scheduled Tribes: Appointed by the President; As prescribed under the constitutional framework; Safeguards concerning Scheduled Tribes.
National Commission for Backward Classes: Appointed by the President; As prescribed under the constitutional framework; Safeguards concerning socially and educationally backward classes.
State Election Commissioner: Appointed by the Governor; Service conditions prescribed by the Governor subject to constitutional safeguards; Supervises Panchayat and Municipal elections.
State Finance Commission: Constituted by the Governor; Constituted every five years; Reviews the financial position of local bodies.
The Constituent Assembly first met on or in 9 December 1946; Sachchidananda Sinha served as temporary President.
Rajendra Prasad became permanent President of the Constituent Assembly on or in 11 December 1946; He presided over the Assembly's constitutional work.
The Objectives Resolution was moved on or in 13 December 1946; Jawaharlal Nehru moved the resolution.
The Objectives Resolution was adopted on or in 22 January 1947; It helped frame the constitutional vision.
The Drafting Committee was appointed on or in 29 August 1947; B. R. Ambedkar chaired the committee.
The Constitution was adopted on or in 26 November 1949; This date is commemorated as Constitution Day.
Most provisions of the Constitution came into force on or in 26 January 1950; India became a republic.
The Indian Independence Act received royal assent on or in 18 July 1947; It provided for two independent dominions.
The National Flag was adopted by the Constituent Assembly on or in 22 July 1947; Its design includes the Ashoka Chakra.
The National Anthem was adopted on or in 24 January 1950; Jana Gana Mana was formally recognised.
The first general elections were held on or in 1951–1952; The Election Commission organised elections based on adult suffrage.
The States Reorganisation Act was passed on or in 1956; It reorganised State boundaries extensively.
Andhra State was formed on or in 1953; It was carved out of the Madras State.
The Planning Commission was established on or in 1950; It was an executive body rather than a constitutional body.
NITI Aayog was established on or in 2015; It replaced the Planning Commission.
The Reserve Bank of India began operations on or in 1935; It was established under the RBI Act, 1934.
The Reserve Bank of India was nationalised on or in 1949; It became publicly owned after Independence.
Fourteen major commercial banks were nationalised on or in 1969; A further six were nationalised in 1980.
The national emergency based on internal disturbance began on or in 1975; The relevant expression was later replaced by armed rebellion.
The Right to Information Act was enacted on or in 2005; It enables access to information held by public authorities subject to legal exemptions.
The Consumer Protection Act currently replacing the 1986 Act was enacted on or in 2019; It provides consumer protection institutions and remedies.
The National Food Security Act was enacted on or in 2013; It creates specified food-security entitlements.
The Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act was enacted on or in 2005; It guarantees specified rural employment on demand subject to the Act.
The Right of Children to Free and Compulsory Education Act was enacted on or in 2009; It supports the constitutional right under Article 21A.
The Protection of Human Rights Act was enacted on or in 1993; It provides for human-rights commissions.
The Comptroller and Auditor-General's Duties, Powers and Conditions of Service Act was enacted on or in 1971; It elaborates the CAG's statutory functions.
The Representation of the People Act on qualifications and electoral rolls was enacted on or in 1950; A separate 1951 Act deals with election conduct and disputes.
The Representation of the People Act on election conduct was enacted on or in 1951; It covers qualifications, disqualifications, conduct and election petitions.
The Panchayati Raj system was inaugurated in Nagaur on or in 1959; Rajasthan became an early pioneer of democratic decentralisation.
The National Human Rights Commission was established on or in 1993; It is a statutory body.
In Indian public affairs, Habeas corpus means A court order requiring production of a detained person to examine the legality of detention.

In Indian public affairs, Quo warranto means A judicial inquiry into the legal authority to hold a public office.
In Indian public affairs, Judicial review means Examination of legislative or executive action for constitutional validity.
In Indian public affairs, Rule of law means Government according to law with legal accountability rather than arbitrary power.
In Indian public affairs, Separation of powers means Distribution of legislative, executive and judicial functions.
In Indian public affairs, Checks and balances means Institutional controls that limit misuse of governmental power.
In Indian public affairs, Parliamentary government means An executive politically responsible to the legislature.
In Indian public affairs, Collective responsibility means The Council of Ministers standing or falling together before the elected House.
In Indian public affairs, Individual ministerial responsibility means A minister's responsibility for the administration of the assigned department.
In Indian public affairs, Federalism means Constitutional distribution of powers between levels of government.
In Indian public affairs, Cooperative federalism means Union and State governments working together on shared concerns.
In Indian public affairs, Residuary legislative power in India means Parliament's authority over matters not enumerated in the three legislative lists.
In Indian public affairs, Concurrent List means Subjects on which both Parliament and State legislatures can legislate, subject to constitutional rules.
In Indian public affairs, Union List means Legislative subjects principally assigned to Parliament.
In Indian public affairs, State List means Legislative subjects principally assigned to State legislatures, subject to constitutional exceptions.
In Indian public affairs, Single citizenship means Indian citizenship without a separate State citizenship.
In Indian public affairs, Secularism in the Indian constitutional setting means Equal civic standing and State respect for freedom of religion, subject to constitutional limits.
In Indian public affairs, Republic means A polity whose head of State does not hold office by hereditary succession.
In Indian public affairs, Universal adult suffrage means Voting rights for adult citizens subject to lawful electoral qualifications.
In Indian public affairs, First-past-the-post election means The candidate with the most votes in a constituency wins.
In Indian public affairs, Proportional representation means An electoral design intended to reflect support in the distribution of seats.
In Indian public affairs, Single transferable vote means A preference-voting method using transfers under specified counting rules.
In Indian public affairs, Secret ballot means Voting that protects the voter's choice from disclosure.
In Indian public affairs, Electoral roll means The official list of registered voters for an electoral area.
In Indian public affairs, Delimitation means The process of drawing or redrawing electoral constituency boundaries.
In Indian public affairs, Reserved constituency means A constituency where candidature is restricted to a specified eligible category.
In Indian public affairs, By-election means An election held to fill a vacancy between general elections.
In Indian public affairs, NOTA means An option expressing that the voter prefers none of the listed candidates.
In Indian public affairs, Model Code of Conduct means Agreed electoral conduct norms administered by the Election Commission.
In Indian public affairs, Election petition means The legal proceeding used to challenge an election under the applicable law.
In Indian public affairs, Whip means A party direction to its legislators concerning attendance or voting.
In Indian public affairs, Anti-defection law means Rules concerning disqualification for specified party-switching conduct.
In Indian public affairs, Question Hour means A parliamentary period for members to question ministers.

In Indian public affairs, Censure motion means A motion criticising specified policies or actions of the government.
In Indian public affairs, Cut motion means A proposal to reduce a demand for a grant during budget discussion.

In Indian public affairs, Government Bill means A Bill introduced by a minister.
In Indian public affairs, Ordinance means A temporary law promulgated by the President or Governor when constitutional conditions are met.
In Indian public affairs, Delegated legislation means Detailed rules made under authority conferred by a parent statute.
